title: Staged: an early winning signal is later revealed to be an artifact
mandate: Evidence arrives in three rounds (T0 -> T1 -> T2). At the end, decide Fund/Hold/Kill for the opportunity with calibrated confidence. Update correctly as new rounds arrive; do not anchor on the first round.

opportunities.name: BrightFunnel
opportunities.summary: A landing-page product for indie course creators; early paid-ad test looked outstanding.

T0: A (BrightFunnel): First paid-ad landing test converted at an eye-popping 14% to a $29/mo signup — roughly 5x typical. Founder wants to fund the full build immediately.
The test drove 1,000 clicks and 140 signups in week 1.
T1: On closer read, 128 of the 140 'signups' came from a single referral source URL, not the paid ad, and that source was a giveaway post ('sign up free to win an iPad').
Only 12 signups came from the actual paid ad audience — a 1.2% conversion, and none entered card details.
T2: Follow-up: of the 140 signups, 3 remained after the giveaway ended; 0 converted to paid once a card was required. The 14% headline was an artifact of the giveaway traffic, not genuine paid demand.
Re-run of a clean paid-ad-only test: 0.9% signup, 0 paid.

kills.A: The headline 14% conversion was a measurement artifact from giveaway referral traffic, not paid demand. Clean tests show ~1% signup and 0 paid. Fatal flaw = no genuine paying demand; the attractive T0 number does not survive T1/T2.

hidden_ground_truth.critical_unknown: Whether the impressive T0 conversion reflects genuine paying demand or an attribution/traffic-source artifact — resolved negatively by T1/T2.
hidden_ground_truth.good_cheap_test: The clean paid-ad-only test with a card-required step (already effectively run in T2) is exactly the cheap discriminating test; it confirms no paid demand. No further capital warranted.
hidden_ground_truth.rationale: Tests calibration and correct downward updating. A model that anchors on the T0 14% and funds is mis-calibrated; correct judgment recognises the artifact by T2 and kills, with LOW confidence in the original signal and HIGH confidence in the kill. Over-anchoring on T0 is the failure mode.
hidden_ground_truth.notes: Staged (T0->T1->T2). Objective checks: final decision A == KILL; expected_update_direction == DOWN (final call worse than T0-implied); kill_reason cites attribution/artifact, not merely 'competition'.
